newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex called to open lower.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were called to open 20 to 25 cents lower, while unleaded gasoline and heating oil were seen opening 0.35 to 0.50 cent lower, tracking overnight weakness in London's markets.
July crude closed down 23 cents at $21.63 a barrel on Friday, while gasoline was down 0.01 at 66.92 cents a gallon and heating oil down 0.28 at 57.52 cents.
Traders said there was little fundamenatal news over the long holiday weekend to lend direction to the market.

Technically-led trading is expected to be the order of the day ahead of the American Petroleum Institute's weekly inventory report, due a day late on Wednesday afternoon because of the holiday, traders said.
IPE Brent crude was down 26 cents at $19.74 a barrel as of 0821 EDT/1237 GMT.

Unleaded gasoline's influence on the complex will also be watched, especially with the unofficial start this past weekend to summer and peak "driving season." The months preceding Memorial Day have seen over the previous five years substantial stock building in anticipation of a rise in gasoline demand. But that stock building has so far failed to materialize this year.
Gasoline futures remained firm for most of last week, and analysts said last week that any move in unleaded would have to come soon for the product to see any appreciable price gain.
